title: Ruler marked in centimetres (or the printed paper ruler)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Spring 2: Place value within 50; length and height; mass and volume
source: Seeded from mathematics/y1 lessons 40, 41 (Ruler marked in centimetres (or the printed paper ruler))
intro: To understand how to measure length in centimetres with a ruler

blocks.text: Cut out a ruler. Each space is 1 cm on a true-size print; check yours against a real ruler, as some printers shrink the page.

questions.model: Teacher lines up the crayon at 0 and reads 9: 9 cm.

questions.q: A rubber starts at 0 and ends at 4. How long?
Which is longer: 10 cm or 7 cm?
Which is longer: 11 cm or 16 cm? By how much?
questions.model: Teacher counts on from 11: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. That is 5 jumps.

questions.q: 8 cm and 8 cm: which is longer?
Measure a spoon, a pencil and a sock in cm.
questions.model: Teacher measures a spoon: start at 0, read 15: 15 cm.

questions.q: A ribbon is 6 cm. Another is 11 cm. Which is longer?
A pencil starts at 2 and ends at 9. How long is it?
A spoon is 15 cm. A fork is 18 cm. How much longer is the fork?
questions.model: Teacher counts on from 15 to 18: 3 jumps, 3 cm.

questions.q: A ribbon is 5 cm longer than a 10 cm pencil. How long is it?
A key starts at 0 and ends at 5. How long?
Big question: why do we all use the same ruler?
questions.a: Centimetres are the same for everyone, so we agree

questions.q: Which is shorter: 9 cm or 13 cm?
Big question: how much longer is 15 cm than 9 cm?
